system.description:
By holding the skull or brain of a recently deceased individual, the necromancer gains a mental image of the last thing to cross that individual's vision. This is an early, primitive fledgling use of the Giovanni family's necromantic art, taught in fragments to a handful of non-Giovanni Cappadocians before Necromancy fully matured as a Discipline.

System: The necromancer must hold either the brain or skull of the dead. Win a Mental Challenge (retest with Occult); the challenge is harder if the remains are more than a fortnight old. This power will not work if the subject had attained Golconda. The degree of victory determines the clarity of the vision, from a hazy sense of how the subject died to an infallible, picture-perfect vision of the cause of death, the killer, and the scene. A botch yields utterly false information.
system.source: Clanbook: Cappadocian, Chapter Three: Observations and Conclusions
